status: Test-only characterization prepared; no Apple execution and no production compatibility approval.

primaryBindings.finding: Public Apple contract places user-script injection after document-element creation and before other content; no runtime observation is claimed.
Public content-world initializer permits explicit page world; legacy initializer documents page-world equivalence.
Public evaluateJavaScript selects native run-as-Program in page world; callAsyncJavaScript chooses the distinct async-function path.
Native script execution checks its execution boundary then evaluates Program source directly, without invoking the page eval function.
Eval permission is mutable state on the same window global object.
Installed CSP can disable eval after policy processing; a previously captured function is not an exemption.
Indirect/captured eval checks Trusted Types and current evalEnabled before executing an indirect eval in global scope. Capturing eval also does not make its declaration scope equal to a Program.
Native result is extracted from the same page-world execution; the public API does not expose an opaque reusable JavaScript value handle.
Object properties are projected into an extracted dictionary container. The test makes no assertion that Foundation dictionary iteration preserves original JavaScript order.
Native API dictionaries and arrays are reconstructed containers. The proposed path obtains a JSON string before this projection.

inferenceNotAppleExecution.candidateRoute: Capture original JSON.stringify in a randomized global lexical const at document start. For a known single expression, native Program evaluates capturedEncoder((expression)) once and returns the JSON string before object-to-Foundation projection.
inferenceNotAppleExecution.conservativeFutureAdmission: A future production integration would need exact original parser recognition of a single ExpressionStatement; arbitrary multi-statement completion is outside this prototype and cannot be silently wrapped or re-evaluated.
inferenceNotAppleExecution.captureEvalRoute: Retained only as an explicit counterexample: the restrictive CSP page is expected to reject captured eval, and permissive eval declarations have different lifetimes from native Program declarations.

testDesign.network: Only loadHTMLString with owned inline markup and CSP default-src none. No URLRequest, source HTTP owner, real credentials, or private account data.
singleExpressionVectors: distinct composed/decomposed Unicode keys checked by UTF8 bytes
one increment and one result evaluation
testDesign.nativeProjection: Checks only values of one native dictionary; deliberately does not assert dictionary enumeration order or manufacture a loss observation.
testDesign.completionOwnership: Each evaluation awaits its real callback. Close seals new evaluations, stops loading, drains outstanding actual evaluation callbacks, removes this probe delegate/scripts. No timer-based settle, polling, global hook, or fake ACK.
limits: Finite owned scripts only; no assertion of forced termination of an infinite page script.
An initial navigation timeout fails the test; cleanup stopLoading does not claim WebContent-process termination.
This is a standalone public-WK characterization inside the existing Native XCTest source, not product-service/JVM/owner validation.

proofLimits: Pinned open-source WebKit is source evidence, not proof of the implementation shipped in any particular iOS SDK/device.
All behavioral assertions are pending. A failing characterization must be retained and diagnosed rather than relabeled as support.
The current production ordered-object branch remains typed unsupported. This candidate never changes it.

The expression route is not claimed equivalent for arbitrary scripts, global declaration semantics, eval/with/dynamic parsing, exceptions, proxies/getters/toJSON, hostile intrinsic mutation, or all current source bridge combinations.
No Node vm code-generation flag or synthetic evaluator is used as WebKit CSP evidence.
Current five control files, App463/466, Package selection and cloud execution are untouched.
